# Frontend design

## Before you build
Commit to one aesthetic direction before writing code. Name it in
a sentence: the tone, the type pairing and the one detail someone
will remember.

Decide what the interface is for before deciding how it looks.
Write down who uses it, on what device, and what they came to do.
Avoid defaults you didn't choose: stock fonts, even spacing and a
palette with no point of view.

## Choosing colour
Pick a dominant colour and one sharp accent. Evenly spread palettes read as timid.
Check contrast at the end.

## Typography
Pair one expressive display face with a quiet text face.
Set body text at 16px or larger on screens, with a line height near 1.5.
Limit the scale to four or five sizes and use weight for emphasis.

## Layout
Use one spacing scale and stick to it.
Let the most important element be the largest thing on the page.
Group related controls and separate unrelated ones with space, not lines.

## Motion
Animate only what helps people follow a change.
Keep transitions under 200 milliseconds and respect reduced motion.

## Details
Check empty, loading and error states as carefully as the happy path.

## Review
Look at the result at 1280 and 390 pixels wide.
Remove anything that doesn’t serve the direction you chose.
Run through references/old-checklist.md before you hand off.

# Frontend design

## Before you build
Commit to one aesthetic direction before writing code. Name it in
a sentence: the tone, the type pairing and the one detail someone
will remember.

Decide what the interface is for before deciding how it looks.
Write down who uses it, on what device, and what they came to do.
Avoid defaults you didn't choose: stock fonts, even spacing and a
palette with no point of view.

## Choosing colour
Pick a dominant colour and one sharp accent. Evenly spread palettes read as timid.
Check contrast while you choose colours, not at the end: body
text needs 4.5:1, large text and icons 3:1.

## Typography
Pair one expressive display face with a quiet text face.
Set body text at 16px or larger on screens, with a line height near 1.5.
Limit the scale to four or five sizes and use weight for emphasis.

## Layout
Use one spacing scale and stick to it.
Let the most important element be the largest thing on the page.
Group related controls and separate unrelated ones with space, not lines.

## Motion
Animate only what helps people follow a change.
Keep transitions under 200 milliseconds and respect reduced motion.

## Details
Check empty, loading and error states as carefully as the happy path.

## Review
Look at the result at 1280 and 390 pixels wide.
Reach every control with the keyboard alone, and check that
focus is always visible.
See references/accessibility.md for the full checklist.
Remove anything that doesn’t serve the direction you chose.

# Accessibility checklist

- Text contrast is at least 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text and icons.
- Every control can be reached and used with the keyboard alone.
- Focus is always visible and moves in reading order.
- Interactive targets are at least 44 by 44 pixels on touch screens.
- Motion respects the reduced motion setting.
- Images that carry meaning have text alternatives.
